question: Which edit grouping and replay rules preserve user intent, and can competing history owners be removed?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 13. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One user-visible undo and redo order across ordinary edits and server-first comment creation; a refused external replay leaves the branch head unchanged.
Invalid session-effect authoring (session replay on a shared effect, orphan callback) is rejected by TypeScript and runtime validation.
One grouping authority interprets native and composition intent; one mounted owner dispatches replay and focus repair.
Plate keeps its configure/store contract over one Plite recorder; no duplicate recorder or history-specific configuration channel.
Undo never silently skips or discards a blocked entry; edits are never locked while a replay is pending.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 09-15 transaction probes, the 09-16 configuration Stop, the 09-23 lifecycle and identity-bridge analysis, and the 09-24 implementation receipt (strict Plite gate, History, React, Yjs and Comments suites) as historical proof. Rechecked on the live tree the local and shared effect type union, the Comments session effect, the replayNow claim, await and settle flow, the removed public names, the native grouping annotation, the mounted dispatch path, the Plate HistoryPlugin adapter, and the dnd plan's T8 and T9 findings. No tests or browser ran.
summary: The job is one undo order across document edits and server-first comment creation, with native grouping, exact selection and root ownership, collaboration and authored conflicts handled honestly. Live Plite types restrict history: { replay } to local effects, BaseCommentsPlugin is its only production author, and replayNow claims the head, awaits the owner and settles applied or blocked through private annotations. Native grouping is an annotation the history merge policy interprets (the React idle timer is gone), mounted undo goes through one runtime.dispatchHistory owner, and Plate's HistoryPlugin forwards live store getters into one Plite recorder. The strongest deletion, dropping the async session lifecycle and making undo synchronous, loses the user-required A/B/C order with server-first comment persistence; a Comments-only stack recreates two shortcut owners. The one unresolved question is recovery from a permanently blocked head (comment owner refusal or authored conflict wedges earlier undo, as the dnd plan's T9 confirms); it was deliberately split off as a product decision with the barrier as the safe default, and no reported failure or clear better semantics exists yet.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted design is selected. Every remaining noun (Promise undo and redo, pending state, request-to-claim map, mounted dispatcher, Plate adapter) prevents a recorded failure.

Deleting the async session lifecycle and restoring synchronous undo is rejected. Server-first comment replay can await or refuse before the branch may move, so sync success would lie or need unsafe compensation.
Removing comment creation from editor history, or giving Comments its own stack, is rejected. It breaks the user-required shared order or creates a second shortcut owner.

Deleting Plate HistoryPlugin and re-exporting Plite history is rejected. A captured history(options) closure cannot take Plate's live configure and store state, so Plate would lose its configuration contract.

Adding an explicit skip or discard action for a permanently blocked head is not pursued. It is the deliberately split product decision, the barrier is the accepted safe default, and no user report or clearly better semantics (discard redo, conflict resolution) exists to choose one.
proofLimits: Source review only; no tests, browser, device IME or collaboration runs. The 09-24 receipt is historical; changed inputs since then were not replayed. Recovery from a permanently blocked head stays an unmade product decision, not proven safe or harmful. The history decision page does not yet reconcile the three dnd executions (ledger conflicts unreconciled-execution). Uncommitted Plite React files from other sessions (composition-state, mutation-controller, typed-text) were not relied on.
